papers.title: PP2A and CDK16 antagonistically regulate WIPI2B phosphorylation and neuronal autophagosome biogenesis.
papers.summary: This paper investigates how two enzymes, PP2A (a phosphatase) and CDK16 (a kinase), work in opposite directions to control the phosphorylation state of WIPI2B, a protein crucial for building autophagosomes. Autophagosomes are the membrane structures that engulf damaged cellular components, including mitochondria, for degradation via autophagy. The study shows this phosphorylation balance is particularly important for regulating autophagosome formation in neurons, linking kinase/phosphatase signaling to neuronal quality-control pathways.
papers.why: Understanding the molecular machinery controlling neuronal autophagosome biogenesis is directly relevant to the mitophagy/autophagy focus of this PhD project, since WIPI2B regulation likely intersects with mitophagy initiation in neurons.

papers.title: OT-knn: A neighborhood-aware optimal transport framework for aligning spatial transcriptomics data.
papers.summary: OT-knn is a new computational method that improves how spatial transcriptomics datasets from different samples or sections can be aligned with each other. It combines optimal transport, a mathematical technique for matching data points efficiently, with nearest-neighbor information so that alignment respects local tissue neighborhoods rather than just global similarity. This should make comparisons across spatial datasets more accurate, especially in tissues with complex, heterogeneous cell arrangements like the brain.
papers.why: Since this PhD project relies heavily on spatial transcriptomics to map neurons, interneurons, and perineuronal nets, a more accurate alignment tool could directly improve integration and comparison of spatial datasets across brain samples.
papers.figure: A figure showing alignment accuracy or spatial coherence of cell/tissue neighborhoods before vs. after OT-knn compared to standard optimal transport methods.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics inform mechanistic physiology in non-model animals.
papers.summary: This paper discusses how single-cell and spatial transcriptomics techniques can be applied to non-model animal species to understand their physiology at a mechanistic level. It likely reviews methodological considerations and challenges when working with organisms lacking established genomic references and tools. The focus is on broadening comparative physiology insights beyond traditional model organisms using these emerging technologies.
papers.why: While centered on non-model animals, this paper is relevant to the profile's spatial transcriptomics methodology for studying cell-type-specific physiology, which could inform analogous approaches in brain tissue.

papers.title: β-Amyloid and glutathione dysregulation cooperatively drive lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis in neuron-like cells.
papers.summary: This paper looks at how amyloid-beta buildup and disruptions in glutathione (a key antioxidant) work together to damage neuron-like cells. The combination causes lipid peroxidation, a process where fats in cell membranes get oxidized and become toxic. This drives ferroptosis, a form of iron-dependent cell death distinct from typical apoptosis.
papers.why: Understanding ferroptosis and oxidative damage pathways in neurons is relevant to the profile's interest in neuronal degeneration mechanisms that intersect with mitophagy and autophagy quality control processes.

papers.title: Mitophagy-Related Gene Dysregulation: Links With Telomere Attrition and Impaired Lung Function in Sulfur Mustard-Exposed Veterans.
papers.summary: This study looks at veterans exposed to sulfur mustard gas and examines whether genes related to mitophagy (the process cells use to clear damaged mitochondria) are abnormally regulated. It connects these gene changes to telomere shortening, a marker of cellular aging, and to reduced lung function. The findings suggest that chemical exposure may accelerate cellular aging processes through disrupted mitochondrial quality control, contributing to chronic lung damage.
papers.why: While focused on lung tissue rather than brain, this paper offers indirect relevance by reinforcing links between mitophagy gene dysregulation and cellular aging/damage markers, which may inform how similar pathways are studied in neurons.

papers.title: Mitophagy-driven immune evasion in skin cancer: multidimensional regulatory networks and context-dependent therapeutic strategies-a narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines how mitophagy, the selective removal of damaged mitochondria, helps skin cancer cells evade immune detection. It discusses the molecular regulatory networks that control this process and how they vary depending on tumor context. The paper also proposes therapeutic strategies that could target mitophagy pathways to improve immune-based treatments for skin cancer.
papers.why: While focused on skin cancer rather than neurons, this review's insights into mitophagy regulatory mechanisms could inform mechanistic parallels relevant to studying mitophagy dysfunction in neurons and interneurons.

papers.title: Modified Hu-lu-ba-wan and its active component trigonelline ameliorate diabetic renal tubular injury via enhancing PACS2-regulated mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contacts and mitophagy.
papers.summary: This study investigates a traditional Chinese medicine formula (Modified Hu-lu-ba-wan) and its active compound trigonelline for treating kidney tubule damage in diabetes. The researchers found that these treatments work by boosting PACS2, a protein that helps maintain contact points between mitochondria and the endoplasmic reticulum. This improved mitochondria-ER communication enhances mitophagy (the clearance of damaged mitochondria), protecting kidney cells from diabetic injury.
papers.why: While focused on kidney rather than brain tissue, this paper's mechanistic insights into PACS2-regulated mitochondria-ER contacts driving mitophagy could inform understanding of analogous organelle contact site regulation relevant to neuronal mitophagy research.
